title: Per-cohort MRV token savings projections (scratchpad)
summary: Scratchpad to estimate per-cohort marginal revenue value (MRV) impact of token-cost levers for Hosted API. Focused on TTL/caching, model-routing, and quantization by customer cohort. Contains scenario projections, assumptions, and quick sensitivity tables.
content:
Goal:
Quickly estimate incremental margin uplift by cohort (MRV) from a handful of operational levers, so Product/Finance can prioritize implementation order for H1. This is an exploratory sheet — values are rough, flagged, and I/O to the canonical unit-econ workbook will follow once we converge on the assumptions.

Scope / cohorts defined (working):
- Free-tier micro (FT-M): lightweight queries, median tokens per request ~40, high churn, prefix cache high-hit potential.
- Startup / SMB self-serve (SMB): median tokens ~120, session affinity moderate, 30% long-running sessions.
- Core SaaS customers (CORE): median tokens ~450, SLAs, lower cache hit but high volume per customer.
- Enterprise latency-sensitive (ENT-L): median tokens ~700, strict latency SLO, limited willingness to quantize.

Key levers evaluated (short):
1) Prefix/KV caching TTL adjustments (edge vs origin): reduce generated tokens by cache-hit fraction.
2) Model routing to lower-cost family for non-latency-critical slices (fallbacks/approx models).
3) Quantization profiles: fp16 vs int8-like quantizations with small quality delta per cohort.
4) Batching policy tweaks per cohort: increase batching window for non-interactive workloads.

Top-level assumptions (baseline):
- Baseline per-token variable cost (amortized + infra + license) by model family: L-family = $0.00008/token, M-family = $0.000045/token, S-family = $0.00002/token.
- Average tokens per request by cohort (median): FT-M=40, SMB=120, CORE=450, ENT-L=700.
- Request volume (monthly requests): FT-M=4,000,000; SMB=1,200,000; CORE=250,000; ENT-L=40,000.
- Baseline prefix-cache hit rates: FT-M 35%, SMB 12%, CORE 6%, ENT-L 3%. TTL change potential: +15pp for FT-M, +8pp SMB, +4pp CORE, +0pp ENT-L.
- Model routing fallback: 18% of CORE traffic flagged as quality-tolerant; 6% ENT-L; 40% FT-M; 28% SMB. Fallback reduces per-token cost to next cheaper family.
- Quantization savings: moving M->quantized M yields 35% per-token cost reduction vs M baseline; quality delta acceptable for FT-M/SMB; risky for ENT-L.
- Increase batching for CORE by 10% reduces effective per-token cost by 8% (due to GPU packing efficiency).

Note: I used blended baseline PPKs above for early sketch (FT/SMB on M-family mix, CORE/ENT on L-family mix). Will break out by model family once we map traffic to model-id.

Scenario A: Aggressive cache TTL + quantize SMB slice
- Action: Raise TTL on common prefixes (edge) -> expected incremental hit +8pp SMB, +15pp FT-M.
- Action: Quantize 60% of SMB requests (non-interactive) -> per-token -35% for that subset.
Projected incremental monthly savings (sketch):
- SMB cache: incremental tokens saved = 144M * 0.08 = 11.52M tokens -> $518 reduction at $0.000045/token baseline.
- SMB quantize: quantized tokens = 144M * 0.6 = 86.4M -> saving = 86.4M * 0.000045 * 0.35 = $1,360
- FT-M cache: 160M * 0.15 = 24M tokens -> $1,080 (assuming M-family price)
- Total rough monthly save ~ $2,958 (~11.9% of baseline SMB+FT-M COGS)

Scenario B: Routing + batching for CORE
- Action: Tag 18% CORE traffic as tolerant -> route to M-family, per-token drops from 0.00008 to 0.000045 for that subset.
- Action: Batching policy: 10% batching improvement across CORE -> 8% per-token effective reduction across remaining CORE traffic.
Projected CORE savings:
- Routed tokens = 112.5M * 0.18 = 20.25M -> per-token delta 0.000035 -> $708 savings
- Batching applied to remainder tokens = 92.25M -> 8% reduction -> $743 savings
- Total CORE monthly save ~ $1,451 (~16% of CORE COGS)

Scenario C: Conservative enterprise playbook (ENT-L)
- Focus on SLAs: no quantize, no routing. Micro-ops: optimize KV cache misses by 2pp only.
- Savings small: 28M * 0.02 = 0.56M tokens -> $44 monthly.

Combined run (A+B): combined monthly savings ~ $4,409 -> annualized ~$52.9k. Implementation effort estimate:
- TTL engineering (edge): 1.5 eng-sprints (infra + experiments)
- Quantization rollout (SMB): 2 eng-sprints + 1 week evaluation per model family
- Model-routing infra: 1 sprint for policy flags + 2 sprints for safe fallbacks + monitoring
- Batching tuning for CORE: 0.5 sprint + perf testing
Total ~ 7–8 sprints cross-team, ~2.5 engineer-months calendar (rough).

Risks / open items (TODOs):
- Quality guardrails: need golden prompt evals per cohort to validate quantize/routing decisions (link to eval harness TODO).
- Attribution of current model family mix by cohort (we need sample of 7 days of model-id telemetry).
- Edge cache budget impact: warming costs and storage egress estimates missing.
- Enterprise SLAs/legal: check if fallback routing allowed under existing enterprise contracts.

Quick sensitivity table (monthly savings vs parameter changes):
Parameter,Low,Base,High

SMB quantize uptake (% of tokens),30,60,90 -> savings($),680,1360,2040
CORE routing (% traffic),8,18,30 -> savings($),314,708,1188
CORE batching eff (%),4,8,12 -> savings($),371,743,1114

Recommended immediate next steps (MVP roadmap):
1) Telemetry pull: export 7d sample mapping cohort -> model-id -> tokens (owner: Linh)
2) Quick eval set: run 200 golden prompts per cohort through quantized model variants (owner: Jonah)
3) TTL pilot: pick one high-hit FT-M prefix cohort and bump edge TTL for 2 weeks (owner: Diego)
4) Cost projection handoff: translate validated per-token deltas into canonical unit-econ workbook (owner: Asha)

Notes-to-self / rough links:
- Use ppk-sim branch mrv-experiments to run Monte Carlo once we have distribution of tokens/requests.
- Slack thread: #ps-ppk (already pinged Diego for TTL data).

Unresolved questions: list
- How many CORE customers are pinned to L-family only? need mapping.
- Is the edge cache TTL change compatible with GDPR retention requirements?
- What is the real per-token blended baseline for FT-M (we assumed M-family).

End of scratchpad — will formalize into a canonical worksheet after items 1–3 completed.

- 2025-02-03 updated volumes from sample logs and tightened estimates
